sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds is on the first floor of the Cambria County Courthouse, 200 South Center Street, Ebensburg, PA 15931. Call (814) 472-1473. Staff work 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, but recording stops at 3:30 p.m. sharp. The office also answers questions by phone.

Records start in 1804. Documents from 1986 forward are searchable online through the county's Tyler portal. The 1924 to 1985 index lives on a separate historical site, and anything older than 1924 can only be seen in the office. Viewing is free of any subscription, and a print or download costs $0.50 per page.

After recording, staff scan the document and hand it right back. Pay with cash or a check made out to Recorder of Deeds, and call ahead if you want a quote on recording fees or copies. Military discharge papers are recorded and copied free.

The current fee schedule is dated December 1, 2025 and is posted as a PDF on the recorder's page. Staff give exact totals by phone, so call before you mail a package. Two surcharges apply to nearly every sale document.

Cambria County recording charges
ChargeAmount or rule
Act 152 of 2016 fee on all deeds and mortgages$15.00, charged since March 1, 2017
Added charge since December 1, 2025$1.00 on deeds, mortgages, easements, satisfactions, assignments, leases, orders and similar documents
Print or download of an online record$0.50 per page
Recording cutoff3:30 p.m., Monday to Friday
PaymentCash or check payable to Recorder of Deeds

The $1.00 charge also reaches statements of adverse possession, condemnations, awards and bills of sale. If your closing involves anything unusual, ask the office for its fee changes notice, which names every affected document.

Since August 1, 2016, the county Assessment Office has had to approve a Uniform Parcel Identifier certification before many documents can be recorded. That covers deeds, decrees of distribution, awards of real estate, mortgages, rights of way, easements, leases, condemnations, declarations of taking, consents, assignments of leases and rents, sewage and water permits, highway occupancy permits, statements of adverse possession and boundary line agreements. The Recorder refuses these papers without the approval.

The Assessment Office is at 200 South Center Street, phone (814) 472-1451. A UPI staff member sits in the Recorder's office, but approval isn't available from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m. each day. Closers are urged to email documents ahead for pre-approval, using the UPI address on the county page.

  • Send the deed for UPI review before the closing date, not on the day.
  • Keep the parcel description identical to the prior deed.
  • Don't book a closing slot that hinges on approval between 1:00 and 2:00 p.m.

The office takes e-recording for certain document types through Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, CSC Global and ePN, and the recorder's page gives a phone number for each vendor. Paper originals can still be carried to the counter.

The Recorder also collects Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and passes it along. The state charges 1% of the value of the real estate, and local governments may add their own share, so ask the office for the combined rate in your municipality and school district. Some transfers are exempt, including certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy.

The state's Department of Revenue can hold buyer and seller both liable. Decide in the purchase agreement who pays, and confirm that your closing agent has the funds in an accepted form.

The county Tax Claim office collects delinquent school, municipal and county real estate taxes and runs the tax sales. It is at 200 South Center Street, phone (814) 472-1445. The Judicial Tax Sale is held each fall in Courtroom 1 at 10:00 a.m., and bidder registration closes a few days ahead.

Since April 1, 2025, a $250.00 fee is added to the costs of every property sold at an upset, judicial, private or repository sale, under Cambria County Ordinance 5 of 2024. Private sales are capped at 50 properties, and each bidder can list up to four per sale. For the 2025 tax year and later, delinquent school taxes in Cambria Township, Ebensburg Borough and Jackson Township, the Central Cambria School District, are collected by Portnoff Law Associates at (866) 211-9466.

A seller who owes back taxes should order a certification from the Tax Claim office, which takes orders online. Ask what is owed for each tax year before you set a closing date.

The Cambria County Assessment Office keeps property records and values real estate for taxation. It sits in the courthouse at 200 South Center Street, with phone (814) 472-1451 and hours of 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. Millage and tax collection belong to other bodies. The county is a fourth-class county under the General County Assessment Law.

The same office runs the Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion program under Acts 50 and 1, and the Clean and Green preferential assessment program under Act 319. It posts an appeal form, appeal board rules, millage rates and a homestead application, along with appeal hearing schedules. If you plan to appeal before listing, read the board rules first.

  • Assessment Office: values property and takes appeals.
  • Tax Claim office: collects delinquent taxes and holds tax sales.
  • Recorder of Deeds: records the deed and collects transfer tax.

Cambria is an older industrial county, and home prices run far below those in the state's suburban counties. It covers 694 square miles, with Ebensburg as the seat and Johnstown as the largest city. Population was 133,472 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 128,968. For 2020 to 2024 the median home value was $121,000, median gross rent was $739 and the owner rate was 76.4%. About 26.2% of residents are 65 or older. Main roads are US 22, US 219 and US 422, plus PA 36, PA 56 and PA 53.

sections.h2: Getting your deed to the counter
sections.html: Order matters here. First get UPI approval from the Assessment Office, ideally by email ahead of the closing. Then confirm the total with the Recorder's office by phone, adding the $15.00 and $1.00 charges to the base fee. Bring cash or a check payable to Recorder of Deeds, or send the package through an e-recording vendor. Arrive well before 3:30 p.m. Before a sale, also ask the Tax Claim office for a certification so no delinquent tax surprises the closing.

faqs.q: What time does the Cambria County Recorder of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 3:30 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office stays open until 4:00 p.m. The office opens at 9:00 a.m. Monday through Friday. Plan the deed to arrive well before the cutoff.

faqs.q: Does Cambria County charge an extra fee on deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. A $15.00 fee applies to all deeds and mortgages under Act 152 of 2016, in place since March 1, 2017. Since December 1, 2025 an added $1.00 applies to deeds, mortgages, easements and many other documents.

faqs.q: Where can I search Cambria County deeds online?
faqs.a: Records from 1986 to now are on the county's Tyler web portal, linked from the recorder's page. The 1924 to 1985 index is on SearchIQS. Records before 1924 are available only in the office, and printing costs $0.50 per page.

faqs.q: Does a deed in Cambria County need approval before recording?
faqs.a: Yes. Since August 1, 2016 the Assessment Office has to approve the UPI for deeds, mortgages, easements, leases and similar documents. Approval isn't offered from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m., so send the document in advance.

faqs.q: What extra fee does Cambria County add to tax sale costs?
faqs.a: A $250.00 fee is added to the costs of every property sold at an upset, judicial, private or repository sale since April 1, 2025. The charge comes from Cambria County Ordinance 5 of 2024. Call the Tax Claim office at (814) 472-1445 for details.
